match: Within this architectural direction, cross-attention is meaningful only when the participating representations are indexed compatible.

Temporal alignment alone does not determine how the streams should exchange evidence. Global cross-attention at early high-resolution stages would create large attention matrices and would permit unrelated facial regions to interact directly. Local matched-window attention offers a more controlled alternative: approximately co-located spatial and temporal regions interact first, while the shifted-window backbones provide broader contextual propagation across layers. Bidirectional cross-attention further allows appearance evidence to retrieve motion evidence and motion evidence to retrieve appearance evidence, which is relevant when either stream may contain the stronger manipulation cue.
